newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Sterling/mark sets new highs, 2.80 looms.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Sterling/mark sets new highs, 2.80 looms.

text.p: Sterling/mark has powered to fresh 4-1/2 year highs above 2.79 marks again overnight, buoyed by robust dollar/mark and good support on dips below its old ERM floor at 2.7780 during Tuesday's pullback, traders said.
The next target for many is now the psychological 2.80 level but this should provide a cap for now at least, chartists said.

"I feel sterling/mark will eventually feel the pressure from a lower cable and top out but, for now, we would look for the 2.7740-to-2.7940 range holding and have 2.80 as the limit on any intraday spikes above that," said Andy Hart, technical analyst at Standard Chartered Bank.
Hart said that an all-round consolidation of the dollar today should stabilise cable but any move above $1.63 should be sold from here.

At 0721 GMT, the pound was trading at a new 4-1/2-year high at 2.7940/45 up more than 1.5 pfennigs from the close yesterday at 2.7785/95 marks. Against the dollar, it was at $1.6244/54 compared with $1.6245/55 late Tuesday.

Analysts said a sustained break above 2.80 marks, however, would set up a move to resistance levels at 2.8225, the monthly high from September 1992, and about 2.8250, the top of a three-week-old rising channel.
A break under 2.7740 marks could see a retreat as far back as trendline support about 2.7620/00.
A positive signal for the pound was its overnight performance against the yen after a tough resistance about 204.90 was taken out and it has since accelerated to new a new 4-1/2-year high at 205.91.
Others stay bearish sterling despite the recent surge.

"This market is developing all the attributes of a major top," said Hans-Guenter Redeker, analyst at Chase Investment Bank. "Long-term momentum indicators have not confirmed recent highs and the wave structure has been overlapping."
RSI - 14 day: Stg/mark: 65 pct, Stg/dollar: 50 pct
